28/G.goal: Explain how human visual perception of XR scenes, from optical image formation to depth and motion, determines XR display requirements for resolution, intensity, and frame rate.
28/G.achieves: Provides the foundational human-factors and display knowledge needed to understand XR visual hardware, address psycho-physiological issues, and later design or optimize XR systems with confidence.

28/O1.goal: Explain how human-eye optics and VR headset lens setups form a real image on the retina that is perceived as a virtual image.
28/O1.achieves: Gives the learner a physiological and optical foundation for understanding VR display hardware and why engineered lenses are needed to project virtual scenes onto the retina.

28/O2.goal: Describe the perceptual mechanisms that allow depth and motion to be experienced in three-dimensional XR scenes.
28/O2.achieves: Helps the learner understand the human-factors basis of immersion and spatial interaction, preparing them to evaluate how XR experiences represent and move through virtual space.

28/O3.goal: Relate human visual perception constraints to XR display requirements for spatial resolution, intensity, and temporal resolution.
28/O3.achieves: Enables the learner to understand the criteria for resolution, brightness, and frame rate in XR displays and to recognize perceptual artifacts such as aliasing and the screen-door effect when evaluating or optimizing displays.
